# Review instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your review to `review.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your reviewer skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
======
# Sprint Plan

## Sprint 1: Review the pull request in pr/

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (unified diff, base to head). The files before the change are under `pr/base/`, after it under `pr/head/`; `pr/PR.md` is the pull request description and is the implementation report for this sprint.

### Tasks

- [x] Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

### Review scope

The gates review `pr/head.diff` (pass `--diff-file pr/head.diff` to the adversarial review). Cite findings as `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from the `pr/head/` files.

## Success Criteria

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict
======
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-260 — the batch runner and the report (implementers G, H): evals/harness/run-ablation.sh (pre-flight with the DEC-0435 hard gate, freeze and corpus checks, pinned source workt….

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
======
grimoires/loa/a2a/:
sprint-1

grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1:
reviewer.md
======
---
name: "review-sprint"
version: "1.1.0"
description: |
  Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria.
  Reviews actual code, not just reports. Quality gate before security audit.
  Resolves local sprint IDs to global IDs via Sprint Ledger.

arguments:
  - name: "sprint_id"
    type: "string"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    required: true
    description: "Sprint to review (e.g., sprint-1)"
    examples: ["sprint-1", "sprint-2", "sprint-10"]

agent: "reviewing-code"
agent_path: "skills/reviewing-code/"

context_files:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/prd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Product requirements for validation"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sdd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Architecture decisions for alignment check"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Sprint tasks and acceptance criteria"
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares sprint: skip, sprint.md becomes
    # optional — loaded if available but absence doesn't block. Read
    # .run/construct-workflow.json to evaluate this condition.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "sprint"
      gate_value: "skip"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    required: false
    purpose: "Sprint Ledger for ID resolution"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/reviewer.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Engineer's implementation report"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/engineer-feedback.md"
    required: false
    purpose: "Previous feedback to verify addressed"

pre_flight:
  - check: "pattern_match"
    value: "$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    error: "Invalid sprint ID. Expected format: sprint-N (e.g., sprint-1)"

  - check: "script"
    script: ".claude/scripts/validate-sprint-id.sh"
    args: ["$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"]
    store_result: "sprint_resolution"
    purpose: "Resolve local sprint ID to global ID via ledger"

  - check: "directory_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID"
    error: "Sprint directory not found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/reviewer.md"
    error: "No implementation report found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_not_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/COMPLETED"
    error: "Sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id is already COMPLETED. No review needed."

outputs:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Review feedback or approval ('All good')"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint plan (checkmarks added on approval)"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint index (status updated)"

<objective>

<!-- @constraint-generated: end reviewing_code_grants -->
</permission_grants>

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

**MUST self-check**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md --gate review`
and resolve any inconsistency before finishing.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Review (large sprints)

When splitting: `resources/PARALLEL-REVIEW.md` (per-task split, consolidation).
</parallel_execution>

<documentation_verification>
## Documentation Verification (Required)

Before approving, Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-*.md`; status `ACTION_REQUIRED` blocks; no report → run `/validate docs` or verify by hand. Blocking: a CHANGELOG entry per task, a CLAUDE.md entry per new command or skill, comments on security code, an SDD update for a major architecture change. Approval templates: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation Verification.
</documentation_verification>

<subagent_report_check>
## Subagent Report Check

Read the sprint's `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/` before approving. Blocking: architecture-validator `CRITICAL_VIOLATION`, security-scanner `CRITICAL` or `HIGH`, test-adequacy-reviewer `INSUFFICIENT`, goal-validation `GOAL_BLOCKED`. `DRIFT_DETECTED`, security `MEDIUM`/`LOW` and test-adequacy `WEAK` are your discretion. No reports (`/validate` is optional): review manually. Grep commands: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Subagent Report Check.
</subagent_report_check>

<checklists>
Checklists, Red Flags and Mermaid standards: `resources/REFERENCE.md`.
</checklists>

<complexity_review>
## Complexity Review (Required)

Review complexity every time (thresholds, tags: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Complexity). BLOCK approval for a function over 50 lines without justification, nesting over 3 without early returns, over 3 duplicate blocks, or circular dependencies. Tag over-engineering findings `SIMPLICITY[delete|stdlib|native|yagni|shrink]: …`; a `loa:shortcut:` marker with no upgrade trigger is `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`. End an over-engineering pass with `net: -<N> lines possible`, or `Lean already. Ship.` and stop. Never flag the one required acceptance check behind non-trivial logic for deletion (the YAGNI minimum).
</complexity_review>

With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, comment, labels); protocol: `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`.

# Review Sprint

## Purpose

Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria as the Senior Technical Lead. Reviews actual code quality, not just the report. Quality gate before security audit.

## Invocation

```
/review-sprint sprint-1
/review-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `reviewing-code` from `skills/reviewing-code/`.

See: `skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, check prerequisites
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Review**: Read actual code files (not just trust the report)
4. **Feedback Check**: Verify previous feedback items were addressed
5. **Decision**: Approve or request changes
6. **Output**: Write feedback or "All good" to `engineer-feedback.md`
7. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to review (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/engineer-feedback.md` | Feedback or "All good" |
| `grimoires/loa/sprint.md` | Updated with checkmarks on approval |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("All good")

When implementation meets all standards:
- Writes "All good" to `engineer-feedback.md`
- Updates `sprint.md` with checkmarks
- Sets sprint status to `REVIEW_APPROVED`
- Next step: `/audit-sprint sprint-N`

### Changes Required

When issues are found:
- Writes detailed feedback to `engineer-feedback.md`
- Includes file paths, line numbers, fixes
- Sprint status remains `IN_PROGRESS`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to address feedback)

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No review needed |

## Review Standards

The reviewer checks for:
- Sprint task completeness
- Acceptance criteria fulfillment
- Code quality and maintainability
- Comprehensive test coverage
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance issues
- Architecture alignment
- Previous feedback resolution

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/review-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/reviewer.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records review feedback:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Feedback**: `br comments add <task-id> "REVIEW: [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> review-approved` or `needs-revision`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

**MUST self-check**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md --gate review`
and resolve any inconsistency before finishing.
</workflow>

# Review Sprint

## Purpose

Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria as the Senior Technical Lead. Reviews actual code quality, not just the report. Quality gate before security audit.

## Invocation

```
/review-sprint sprint-1
/review-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `reviewing-code` from `skills/reviewing-code/`.

See: `skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, check prerequisites
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Review**: Read actual code files (not just trust the report)
4. **Feedback Check**: Verify previous feedback items were addressed
5. **Decision**: Approve or request changes
6. **Output**: Write feedback or "All good" to `engineer-feedback.md`
7. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to review (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/engineer-feedback.md` | Feedback or "All good" |
| `grimoires/loa/sprint.md` | Updated with checkmarks on approval |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("All good")

When implementation meets all standards:
- Writes "All good" to `engineer-feedback.md`
- Updates `sprint.md` with checkmarks
- Sets sprint status to `REVIEW_APPROVED`
- Next step: `/audit-sprint sprint-N`

### Changes Required

When issues are found:
- Writes detailed feedback to `engineer-feedback.md`
- Includes file paths, line numbers, fixes
- Sprint status remains `IN_PROGRESS`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to address feedback)

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No review needed |

## Review Standards

The reviewer checks for:
- Sprint task completeness
- Acceptance criteria fulfillment
- Code quality and maintainability
- Comprehensive test coverage
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance issues
- Architecture alignment
- Previous feedback resolution

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/review-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/reviewer.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records review feedback:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Feedback**: `br comments add <task-id> "REVIEW: [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> review-approved` or `needs-revision`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

# Adversarial Cross-Model Review — Phase 2.5 mechanics

Referenced from `reviewing-code/SKILL.md` Phase 2.5. Runs when
`flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true` in `.loa.config.yaml`.

**Objective**: Invoke a cross-model dissenter to catch reviewer blind spots before the final decision.

**Steps**:
1. Invoke adversarial review as the bare call the allowlist grants (`--diff-range`: the script runs the `git diff` itself):
   ```bash
   .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type review --sprint-id <sprint_id> \
     --diff-range main...HEAD --context-file <concerns file> --json
   ```
2. Read `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-review.json` (Read tool) and parse its findings:
   - If `findings` is empty: continue to Phase 3 — after triaging any rejected payloads (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, which is mandatory either way
   - If the invocation failed: record it (below) before Phase 3
   - If BLOCKING findings exist: incorporate into Phase 4 decision (forces CHANGES_REQUIRED)
   - If ADVISORY findings only: append as "Cross-Model Observations" section in feedback

**Failure must produce a record.** The `adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks this file before any COMPLETED marker is written (

... [19825 characters truncated] ...

ot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.

**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).
KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.

## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)

- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
  a replacement for the symbol.
- **Budget scaling (`budget_scale`, `budget_cents_max`).** `flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale`
  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.

   963	# post_run <run-dir> <run_id> <task> <task_yaml> <attempts> <retry_reason> <pipeline_status>
   964	#          <override> <row-out> <log> — the chain after a finished pipeline, shared by a trial
   965	# and by --rerow: took-effect, drift guard, grade (completed, agent_error and cap_failure runs
   966	# without an override), then ablation-row.sh into <row-out>. Results in PR_TE (ok | fail |
   967	# skipped), PR_TE_REASON, PR_DRIFT (json or null), PR_EXTRA (the extra models, json),
   968	# PR_GRC (null or the grade exit), PR_RRC (the row exit) and PR_OVERRIDE (the final override)
   969	post_run() {
   970	  local rd="$1" rid="$2" task="$3" tyaml="$4" attempts="$5" rr="$6" st="$7" row_out="$9" plog="${10}"
   971	  PR_OVERRIDE="$8" PR_TE=skipped PR_TE_REASON="" PR_DRIFT=null PR_EXTRA='{}' PR_GRC=null PR_RRC=0
   972	  if [[ -z "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]]; then
   973	    case "$st" in
   974	      completed|agent_error|cap_failure)
   975	        local trc=0 tout dout id
   976	        tout="$("$TOOK_BIN" --run-dir "$rd" --suite-file "$SUITE_FILE" 2>&1)" || trc=$?
   977	        printf '%s\n' "$tout" >> "$plog"
   978	        if [[ $trc -eq 0 ]]; then PR_TE=ok
   979	        else
   980	          PR_TE=fail PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error
   981	          PR_TE_REASON="took-effect exit $trc: $(grep -E ' FAIL' <<<"$tout" | head -4 | cut -c1-200 | tr '\n' ';' || true)"
   982	        fi
   983	        dout="$(drift_check "$rd" "$rid" 2>>"$plog" || true)"
   984	        PR_DRIFT="$(sed -n 1p <<<"$dout")" PR_EXTRA="$(sed -n 2p <<<"$dout")"
   985	        jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PR_DRIFT" || PR_DRIFT=null
   986	        jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PR_EXTRA" || PR_EXTRA='{}'
   987	        while IFS=$'\t' read -r id labels toks; do
   988	          [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
   989	          printf 'run-ablation: extra model %s in %s (%s output tokens; a WebFetch summariser or built-in subagent, not drift — DEC-0545)\n' \
   990	            "$id" "$labels" "$toks" >> "$plog"
   991	        done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value.phases | join(",")), (.value.output_tokens | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$PR_EXTRA")
   992	        if [[ "$PR_DRIFT" != null ]]; then PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error; printf 'run-ablation: drift %s\n' "$PR_DRIFT" >> "$plog"; fi
   993	        if [[ -z "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]]; then
   994	          local -a g=("$GRADE_BIN" "$rd" "$task" --suite-root "$SUITE_ROOT" --executor "$EXECUTOR" --image "$IMAGE" --docker-bin "$DOCKER_BIN")
   995	          [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && g+=(--tasks-dir smoke)
   996	          PR_GRC=0; "${g[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_GRC=$?
   997	          if [[ $PR_GRC -ne 0 ]]; then PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error; printf 'run-ablation: grade exit %s\n' "$PR_GRC" >> "$plog"; fi
   998	        fi ;;
   999	    esac
  1000	  fi
  1001	  local -a r=("$ROW_BIN" --run-dir "$rd" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --manifest "$MAN_PATH" --attempts "$attempts" --out "$row_out")
  1002	  [[ -n "$rr" ]] && r+=(--retry-reason "$rr")
  1003	  [[ -n "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]] && r+=(--status "$PR_OVERRIDE")
  1004	  "${r[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_RRC=$?
  1005	  return 0
  1006	}

  1008	run_trial() {  # run_trial <jid> <arm> <task> <type> <kind> <trial> <run_id> <task_yaml> <watchdog_s>
  1009	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" task="$3" type="$4" kind="$5" trial="$6" rid="$7" tyaml="$8" wds="$9"
  1010	  local base="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial" tlog="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial.log"
  1011	  local attempt=0 rd="" st="" prc retry_reason="" first_usd=0 sig override="" pid
  1012	  local t0 t1
  1013	  mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
  1014	  t0="$(date +%s)"
  1015	  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
  1016	    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  1017	    rd="$(fresh_dir "$base")"
  1018	    printf '%s\n' "$rd" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.rundir"
  1019	    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wdkill"
  1020	    printf '%s run-ablation: %s attempt %d run_dir %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$attempt" "$rd" >> "$tlog"
  1021	    local -a cmd=("$PIPELINE_BIN" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --arm "$arm" --run-dir "$rd" --run-id "$rid" --trial "$trial"
  1022	                  --source-tree "$TREE" --suite-file "$SUITE_FILE" --executor "$EXECUTOR" --image "$IMAGE"
  1023	                  --docker-bin "$DOCKER_BIN" --max-run-usd "$RUN_CAP")
  1024	    # its own process group, so the watchdog can signal the pipeline and everything under it
  1025	    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then setsid "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
  1026	    else "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
  1027	    fi
  1028	    pid=$!
  1029	    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$pid" "$(date +%s)" "$wds" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
  1030	    prc=0; wait "$pid" || prc=$?
  1031	    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
  1032	    st="$(final_status "$rd")"
  1033	    if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" ]]; then
  1034	      override=interrupted
  1035	      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "watchdog: no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (pipeline exit $prc)"
  1036	      break
  1037	    fi
  1038	    if [[ -z "$st" ]]; then
  1039	      override=interrupted
  1040	      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "no final pipeline record (pipeline exit $prc)"
  1041	      break
  1042	    fi
  1043	    if [[ "$st" == agent_error ]] && sig="$(is_pipeline_transport_failure "$rd")"; then
  1044	      if [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then
  1045	        first_usd="$(jq -r '(.spent_usd // 0) | tonumber? // 0' "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  1046	        retry_reason="transport: ${sig% *} in phase ${sig#* }"
  1047	        printf '%s run-ablation: %s %s; retrying once after %ss into a fresh run dir\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$retry_reason" "$RETRY_WAIT" >> "$tlog"
  1048	        sleep "$RETRY_WAIT"; continue
  1049	      fi
  1050	      override=transport_error
  1051	    fi
  1052	    break
  1053	  done
  1054	  post_run "$rd" "$rid" "$task" "$tyaml" "$attempt" "$retry_reason" "$st" "$override" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" "$tlog"
  1055	  t1="$(date +%s)"
  1056	  jq -n --arg rid "$rid" --arg rd "$rd" --argjson att "$attempt" --arg rr "$retry_reason" --arg first "$first_usd" \
  1057	    --arg pst "${st:-}" --arg ov "$PR_OVERRIDE" --arg te "$PR_TE" --arg ter "$PR_TE_REASON" --argjson drift "$PR_DRIFT" \
  1058	    --argjson grc "$PR_GRC" --argjson rrc "$PR_RRC" --argjson secs "$(( t1 - t0 ))" --argjson extra "$PR_EXTRA" \
  1059	    '{run_id: $rid, run_dir: $rd, attempts: $att, retry_reason: (if $rr == "" then null else $rr end),
  1060	      first_attempt_usd: ($first | tonumber? // 0), pipeline_status: $pst, override: $ov, took_effect: $te,
  1061	      took_effect_reason: $ter, drift: $drift, grade_rc: $grc, row_rc: $rrc, seconds: $secs,
  1062	      extra_models: $extra}' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result.tmp"

  1064	}

   963	# post_run <run-dir> <run_id> <task> <task_yaml> <attempts> <retry_reason> <pipeline_status>
   964	#          <override> <row-out> <log> — the chain after a finished pipeline, shared by a trial
   965	# and by --rerow: took-effect, drift guard, grade (completed, agent_error and cap_failure runs
   966	# without an override), then ablation-row.sh into <row-out>. Results in PR_TE (ok | fail |
   967	# skipped), PR_TE_REASON, PR_DRIFT (json or null), PR_EXTRA (the extra models, json),
   968	# PR_GRC (null or the grade exit), PR_RRC (the row exit) and PR_OVERRIDE (the final override)
   969	post_run() {
   970	  local rd="$1" rid="$2" task="$3" tyaml="$4" attempts="$5" rr="$6" st="$7" row_out="$9" plog="${10}"
   971	  PR_OVERRIDE="$8" PR_TE=skipped PR_TE_REASON="" PR_DRIFT=null PR_EXTRA='{}' PR_GRC=null PR_RRC=0
   972	  if [[ -z "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]]; then
   973	    case "$st" in
   974	      completed|agent_error|cap_failure)
   975	        local trc=0 tout dout id
   976	        tout="$("$TOOK_BIN" --run-dir "$rd" --suite-file "$SUITE_FILE" 2>&1)" || trc=$?
   977	        printf '%s\n' "$tout" >> "$plog"
   978	        if [[ $trc -eq 0 ]]; then PR_TE=ok
   979	        else
   980	          PR_TE=fail PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error
   981	          PR_TE_REASON="took-effect exit $trc: $(grep -E ' FAIL' <<<"$tout" | head -4 | cut -c1-200 | tr '\n' ';' || true)"
   982	        fi
   983	        dout="$(drift_check "$rd" "$rid" 2>>"$plog" || true)"
   984	        PR_DRIFT="$(sed -n 1p <<<"$dout")" PR_EXTRA="$(sed -n 2p <<<"$dout")"
   985	        jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PR_DRIFT" || PR_DRIFT=null
   986	        jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$PR_EXTRA" || PR_EXTRA='{}'
   987	        while IFS=$'\t' read -r id labels toks; do
   988	          [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
   989	          printf 'run-ablation: extra model %s in %s (%s output tokens; a WebFetch summariser or built-in subagent, not drift — DEC-0545)\n' \
   990	            "$id" "$labels" "$toks" >> "$plog"
   991	        done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value.phases | join(",")), (.value.output_tokens | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$PR_EXTRA")
   992	        if [[ "$PR_DRIFT" != null ]]; then PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error; printf 'run-ablation: drift %s\n' "$PR_DRIFT" >> "$plog"; fi
   993	        if [[ -z "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]]; then
   994	          local -a g=("$GRADE_BIN" "$rd" "$task" --suite-root "$SUITE_ROOT" --executor "$EXECUTOR" --image "$IMAGE" --docker-bin "$DOCKER_BIN")
   995	          [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && g+=(--tasks-dir smoke)
   996	          PR_GRC=0; "${g[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_GRC=$?
   997	          if [[ $PR_GRC -ne 0 ]]; then PR_OVERRIDE=infrastructure_error; printf 'run-ablation: grade exit %s\n' "$PR_GRC" >> "$plog"; fi
   998	        fi ;;
   999	    esac
  1000	  fi
  1001	  local -a r=("$ROW_BIN" --run-dir "$rd" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --manifest "$MAN_PATH" --attempts "$attempts" --out "$row_out")
  1002	  [[ -n "$rr" ]] && r+=(--retry-reason "$rr")
  1003	  [[ -n "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]] && r+=(--status "$PR_OVERRIDE")
  1004	  "${r[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_RRC=$?
  1005	  return 0
  1006	}

  1168	PIDS=() PJOB=() PIDX=()
  1169	watchdog_tick() {
  1170	  local j f pid start wds now rd t0
  1171	  now="$(date +%s)"
  1172	  for j in ${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}; do
  1173	    f="$JOBS_DIR/$j.pgid"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
  1174	    read -r pid start wds < "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  1175	    [[ -n "$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE" ]] && wds="$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE"
  1176	    [[ $(( now - start )) -gt $wds ]] || continue
  1177	    rd="$(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$j.rundir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  1178	    [[ -z "$(final_status "$rd")" ]] || continue
  1179	    if [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" ]]; then
  1180	      printf '%s\n' "$now" > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd"
  1181	      log "watchdog: $j has no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (twice its phase-sum timeout); SIGTERM to process group $pid"
  1182	      kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  1183	    elif [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill" ]]; then
  1184	      read -r t0 < "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" || t0="$now"
  1185	      if [[ $(( now - t0 )) -ge $WATCHDOG_GRACE ]]; then
  1186	        : > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill"
  1187	        log "watchdog: $j still running ${WATCHDOG_GRACE}s after SIGTERM; SIGKILL to process group $pid"
  1188	        kill -KILL -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  1189	      fi
  1190	    fi
  1191	  done
  1192	  return 0
  1193	}
  1194	reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
  1195	  local i
  1196	  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
  1197	    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
  1198	      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
  1199	        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
  1200	        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PIDX[$i]}"

  1202	        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PIDX=("${PIDX[@]+"${PIDX[@]}"}")
  1203	        break
  1204	      fi
  1205	    done
  1206	    watchdog_tick

  1233	# --- --rerow: the post-run chain again over a rowed run dir, the row replaced in place ---
  1234	# replace_row_try <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; 1 with REPLACE_ERR set and the rows file
  1235	# untouched (the old row stays). replace_row is the --rerow form: it dies instead
  1236	replace_row_try() {
  1237	  local rid="$1" newf="$2" tmp="$ROWS.rerow.$$" rc=0 vout="" perr
  1238	  REPLACE_ERR=""
  1239	  local -a v=("$ROW_BIN" --validate "$tmp"); [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && v+=(--allow-ungraded)
  1240	  {
  1241	    command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && flock -x 9
  1242	    perr="$(python3 -I - "$ROWS" "$tmp" "$BATCH" "$rid" "$newf" 2>&1 <<'PY'
  1243	import json, sys
  1244	rows, tmp, batch, rid, newf = sys.argv[1:6]
  1245	new = open(newf, encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
  1246	out, n = [], 0
  1247	with open(rows, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
  1248	    for line in fh:
  1249	        try: o = json.loads(line)
  1250	        except ValueError: o = None
  1251	        if isinstance(o, dict) and o.get("batch") == batch and o.get("run_id") == rid:
  1252	            n += 1; out.append(new + "\n")
  1253	        else:
  1254	            out.append(line if line.endswith("\n") else line + "\n")
  1255	if n != 1:
  1256	    print("run_id %s has %d rows" % (rid, n), file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
  1257	with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.writelines(out)
  1258	PY
  1259	)" || rc=$?
  1260	    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
  1261	      vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
  1262	      if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then mv "$tmp" "$ROWS"; else REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$vout" | tail -1)"; fi
  1263	    else
  1264	      REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$perr" | tail -1)"
  1265	    fi
  1266	  } 9>>"$ROWS.lock"
  1267	  rm -f "$tmp"
  1268	  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { REPLACE_ERR="${REPLACE_ERR:-exit $rc}"; return 1; }
  1269	  return 0
  1270	}
  1271	replace_row() {  # replace_row <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; dies (rows file untouched) otherwise
  1272	  replace_row_try "$1" "$2" && return 0
  1273	  printf '%s\n' "$REPLACE_ERR" >&2
  1274	  die "rerow $1: the replacement did not validate or the row moved ($REPLACE_ERR); $ROWS unchanged"
  1275	}

  1329	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r rid st cost deg; do

  1331	      for j in "${!PL_RUN[@]}"; do [[ "${PL_RUN[$j]}" == "$rid" ]] && { k=$j; break; }; done

  1358	  | while IFS= read -r l; do log "$l"; done

  1399	elif [[ $paused_n -gt 0 && $left -gt 0 ]]; then

  1410	fi

1	     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	     2	# =============================================================================
3	     3	# ablation-report.py — the cycle-130 ablation report (PRD FR-8, SDD §5.12, §4.2)
4	     4	#
5	     5	# Reads runs.jsonl rows (SDD §3.1, ablation-row.sh), the batch MANIFEST.json files
6	     6	# (SDD §3.4, run-ablation.sh) and the suite file (evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:
7	     7	# arms[], trials, cut_ladder, priority and the pre-registered `rules` block, D-A5),
8	     8	# applies the pre-registered rules to every component arm (A2 … A7) against the
9	     9	# control a1_full, checks H1 (a1_full vs a0_bare) and the A4 sensitivity rule, and
10	    10	# writes report.md (and a --json twin with the same numbers).
11	    11	#
12	    12	# Usage:
13	    13	#   ablation-report.py --runs F [--runs F ...] --manifests DIR [--manifests DIR ...]
14	    14	#                      --suite F --out report.md [--json report.json]
15	    15	#                      [--seed 20261015] [--resamples N] [--level L]
16	    16	#                      [--exclude-degraded true|false] [--partial]
17	    17	#                      [--cuts F] [--not-run CSV]
18	    18	#
19	    19	# Options:
20	    20	#   --runs F            a runs.jsonl file (repeatable). Every non-blank line is one row
21	    21	#                       and must carry schema_version 1 (an integer, or a "1.x" string);
22	    22	#                       a row with another major, no schema_version, or a line that is not
23	    23	#                       a JSON object stops the report (exit 2, naming file:line and run_id).
24	    24	#                       A run_id seen twice keeps its last row (the earlier one is listed).
25	    25	#   --manifests DIR     a directory searched recursively (symlinks not followed) for
26	    26	#                       MANIFEST.json files (repeatable). Each gives a batch's provenance:
27	    27	#                       batch, arm_map, shuffle_seed, source_commit, suite_manifest_sha256,
28	    28	#                       suite_version, pre_registration_ref, cli_version (top level or
29	    29	#                       executor.cli_version), image_digest, smoke. A manifest with an
30	    30	#                       unknown schema_version major, two manifests claiming one batch, or
31	    31	#                       an arm_map entry disagreeing with a row's arm → exit 2.
32	    32	#   --suite F           the suite file: YAML read through `yq -o=json` (mikefarah yq v4,
33	    33	#                       as arms-report.py does), or JSON when the file parses as JSON.
34	    34	#                       The Method section quotes its `rules:` block verbatim.
35	    35	#   --out F             report.md (the only files written are --out and --json; a symlink
36	    36	#                       at either path is refused)
37	    37	#   --json F            the JSON twin (schema_version 1)
38	    38	#   --seed N            bootstrap seed (default 20261015); every interval uses its own
39	    39	#                       random.Random(seed), so a figure does not depend on which other
40	    40	#                       arms are present
41	    41	#   --resamples N       default rules.bootstrap.resamples (10,000); a value other than the
42	    42	#                       pre-registered one is marked in the header
43	    43	#   --level L           default rules.bootstrap.level (0.90); same marking
44	    44	#   --exclude-degraded  true (default) | false: rows with degraded: true are excluded
45	    45	#                       pairwise (rules.exclusion.statuses names `degraded`)
46	    46	#   --partial           prints "PARTIAL — rows so far, no decision is final"; exit 1 when no
47	    47	#                       comparison (A2–A7, H1, A4) has a valid pair on every primary it uses
48	    48	#   --cuts F            a JSON list of {arm, reason, figure[, state]} the lead recorded;
49	    49	#                       arm is an id (a5_no_flatline) or a label (A5); state is not_run_cut
50	    50	#                       (default) or inconclusive_by_power (a pre-declared power cut)
51	    51	#   --not-run CSV       arm ids or labels read as Not run (cut) with figure "--not-run"
52	    52	#
53	    53	# Row treatment (DEC-0393, DEC-0417):
54	    54	#   not decided, listed  rows of a smoke batch (manifest smoke: true), rows whose batch has
55	    55	#                        no manifest, rows of an arm the suite does not run (absent or
56	    56	#                        unknown), rows on a task type outside the arm's task_types
57	    57	#                        (applicability refusals; not counted in the excluded share)
58	    58	#   excluded pairwise    status in rules.exclusion.statuses plus transport_error and
59	    59	#                        infrastructure_error (DEC-0417), degraded: true (with
60	    60	#                        --exclude-degraded true), and a scoring status whose primary is
61	    61	#                        null (ungraded); the task-trial cell leaves BOTH arms of every
62	    62	#                        comparison it is in; a cell holding a valid row (a rerun) is valid
63	    63	#   cap_failure          0 on every applicable primary (pass rate 0, every defect missed)
64	    64	#   completed, agent_error  score what the row holds (hidden_test_pass_rate; defects)
65	    65	#   The sensitivity figure repeats the comparison with cap_failure excluded pairwise
66	    66	#   instead of scored 0; no decision reads it.
67	    67	#
68	    68	# Statistics (pre-registered in the suite's rules block; formulas in the Method section):
69	    69	#   pass rate unit  the task: per task, the mean over its valid trials, arm minus a1_full
70	    70	#   catch-rate unit the defect: per review-catch task and defect dK, the share of the
71	    71	#                   arm's valid trials that caught it, arm minus a1_full; per-defect ids
72	    72	#                   come from the row's `defects_missed` (or `recall.missed`) list of dK
73	    73	#                   ids when present, else each defect of the task takes the row's
74	    74	#                   defect_catch_rate (aggregate rows); the task-level figure is also
75	    75	#                   reported (rules.bootstrap.also_report) and decides nothing
76	    76	#   interval        percentile bootstrap of the mean paired difference: `resamples`
77	    77	#                   resamples with replacement, linear interpolation between order
78	    78	#                   statistics, [lo, hi] = the (1-level)/2 and 1-(1-level)/2 quantiles
79	    79	#   d               the mean of the paired differences (not the bootstrap mean)
80	    80	#   c, w            cost and wall-clock delta in percent against a1_full,
81	    81	#                   (mean_arm − mean_a1) / mean_a1 × 100, over the per-task means of the
82	    82	#                   cells the primaries paired
83	    83	#   MDE             (z(1−(1−level)/2) + z(0.90)) × sd(paired diffs) / sqrt(n): the smallest
84	    84	#                   true mean difference a paired test at the report level detects with 0.90
85	    85	#                   power at the available n; n < 2 → n/a
86	    86	#   comparisons     every predicate compares values rounded to 9 decimals, so a planted
87	    87	#                   −0.03 reads −0.03 and not −0.030000000000000027
88	    88	#
89	    89	# Decision per arm (rules.predicates, first match, DEC-0416, with DEC-0393's guard first):
90	    90	#   the degradation guard (excluded share > rules.exclusion.inconclusive_above_share →
91	    91	#   inconclusive, labelled Inconclusive-by-degradation, whatever the interval) →
92	    92	#   investigate → keep → inconclusive (d < -0.03 or no valid pair) → remove → simplify. Then: an arm named by --cuts / --not-run reads
93	    93	#   Not run (cut) or Inconclusive-by-power with the lead's figure; an arm whose MDE on an
94	    94	#   applicable primary exceeds rules.mde_cut and whose predicate outcome is remove or
95	    95	#   simplify reads Inconclusive-by-power with the figure (a null result the sample could
96	    96	#   not have detected); A8 (absent: true) reads component-absent with the suite evidence.
97	    97	#
98	    98	# Exit codes:
99	    99	#   0  report written
100	   100	#   1  --partial and no decidable comparison (the report is still written)
101	   101	#   2  usage error, unreadable input, unknown schema major, provenance conflict
102	   102	#
103	   103	# Tested by evals/tests/ablation-report.bats (planted rows generated by
104	   104	# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-report/gen-fixtures.py).

143	   143	def r9(x):

169	   169	    if isinstance(v, bool):

171	   171	    if isinstance(v, int):
172	   172	        return v
173	   173	    if isinstance(v, float) and v.is_integer():
174	   174	        return int(v)

180	   180	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
181	   181	    """Linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy's default 'linear')."""
182	   182	    n = len(sorted_xs)
183	   183	    if n == 0:
184	   184	        return None
185	   185	    pos = q * (n - 1)
186	   186	    lo = int(math.floor(pos))
187	   187	    hi = min(lo + 1, n - 1)
188	   188	    frac = pos - lo
189	   189	    return sorted_xs[lo] + (sorted_xs[hi] - sorted_xs[lo]) * frac
190	   190

192	   192	def bootstrap(diffs, resamples, level, seed):
193	   193	    if not diffs:
194	   194	        return None, None
195	   195	    rng = random.Random(seed)
196	   196	    n = len(diffs)
197	   197	    means = sorted(sum(rng.choices(diffs, k=n)) / n for _ in range(resamples))
198	   198	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
199	   199	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)

202	   202	def mde(diffs, level):
203	   203	    if len(diffs) < 2:
204	   204	        return None
205	   205	    nd = statistics.NormalDist()
206	   206	    z = nd.inv_cdf(1.0 - (1.0 - level) / 2.0) + nd.inv_cdf(POWER)
207	   207	    return z * statistics.stdev(diffs) / math.sqrt(len(diffs))

215	   215	        if m:

217	   217	        else:

222	   222	        if len(ns) == 1:

224	   224	        elif len(ns) >= 3 and ns == list(range(ns[0], ns[-1] + 1)):
225	   225	            out.append(f"{prefix}{ns[0]}…t{ns[-1]}")
226	   226	        else:

378	   378	    def __init__(self, suite, rows, mans, args, cap_excluded):
379	   379	        self.suite, self.rules, self.args = suite, suite["rules"], args
380	   380	        self.cap_excluded = cap_excluded
381	   381	        self.arms = {a["id"]: a for a in suite["arms"] if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("id")}
382	   382	        ex = self.rules.get("exclusion") or {}
383	   383	        self.ex_statuses = set(ex.get("statuses") or []) | set(DEC0417_EXCLUDED)
384	   384	        self.guard = float(ex.get("inconclusive_above_share", 0.25))
385	   385	        self.listed = []        # rows that never enter a decision, with the reason
386	   386	        self.excluded = []      # excluded rows (status/reason), superseded included
387	   387	        self.cells = {}         # (arm, task) -> {trial: {"valid": row|None, "rows": [...]}}
388	   388	        self.task_type = {}
389	   389	        self.task_defects = {}
390	   390	        self.arm_rows = {}
391	   391	        for row in rows:
392	   392	            seeded = row.get("defects_seeded")
393	   393	            if isinstance(seeded, int) and not isinstance(seeded, bool) and seeded > 0:
394	   394	                self.task_defects[row["task_id"]] = max(self.task_defects.get(row["task_id"], 0), seeded)
395	   395	        for row in rows:
396	   396	            self._classify(row, mans)
397	   397	        for (arm, task), trials in self.cells.items():
398	   398	            for t, cell in trials.items():
399	   399	                valid = [x for x in cell["rows"] if x["_valid"]]
400	   400	                cell["valid"] = valid[-1] if valid else None
401	   401	                for x in cell["rows"]:
402	   402	                    if x["_valid"] and x is not cell["valid"]:
403	   403	                        self.excluded.append(self._exrow(x, f"duplicate cell; superseded by {cell['valid']['run_id']}",
404	   404	                                                         counted=False))
405	   405	                    elif not x["_valid"]:
406	   406	                        sup = f"; superseded by {cell['valid']['run_id']}" if cell["valid"] else ""
407	   407	                        self.excluded.append(self._exrow(x, x["_reason"] + sup, counted=not cell["valid"]))

409	   409	    @staticmethod
410	   410	    def _exrow(x, reason, counted):
411	   411	        return {"run_id": x["run_id"], "arm": x["arm"], "task_id": x["task_id"], "trial": x["trial"],
412	   412	                "status": x["status"], "reason": reason, "cell_excluded": counted}

414	   414	    def applies(self, arm, ttype):
415	   415	        types = self.arms[arm].get("task_types") or []
416	   416	        return "all" in types or ttype in types or ("build" in types and ttype in BUILD_TYPES)

418	   418	    def primaries(self, arm):
419	   419	        types = self.arms[arm].get("task_types") or []
420	   420	        pba = self.rules.get("primaries_by_arm") or {}
421	   421	        if "all" in types or REVIEW in types:
422	   422	            return list(pba.get("all_types") or [PASS, CATCH])
423	   423	        return list(pba.get("build_only") or [PASS])

425	   425	    def _classify(self, row, mans):
426	   426	        arm, task, ttype = row["arm"], row["task_id"], row["task_type"]
427	   427	        m = mans.get(row["batch"])
428	   428	        if m is None:
429	   429	            return self.listed.append((row, "no manifest for batch " + row["batch"]))
430	   430	        amap = m.get("arm_map") or {}
431	   431	        if isinstance(amap, dict) and row["run_id"] in amap and amap[row["run_id"]] != arm:
432	   432	            raise Fail(f"{row['_where']}: row {row['run_id']} arm {arm} disagrees with "
433	   433	                       f"{m['_path']} arm_map ({amap[row['run_id']]})")
434	   434	        if m.get("smoke") is True:
435	   435	            return self.listed.append((row, "smoke batch " + row["batch"]))
436	   436	        if arm not in self.arms or self.arms[arm].get("absent"):
437	   437	            return self.listed.append((row, f"arm {arm} is not run by the suite"))
438	   438	        if ttype not in BUILD_TYPES and ttype != REVIEW:
439	   439	            return self.listed.append((row, f"unknown task_type {ttype}"))
440	   440	        if not self.applies(arm, ttype):
441	   441	            return self.listed.append((row, f"not applicable: {arm} does not run {ttype} tasks"))
442	   442	        self.task_type[task] = ttype
443	   443	        self.arm_rows.setdefault(arm, []).append(row)
444	   444	        st = row["status"]
445	   445	        reason = None
446	   446	        if st in self.ex_statuses:
447	   447	            reason = st
448	   448	        elif self.args.exclude_degraded and row.get("degraded") is True:
449	   449	            reason = "degraded: " + str(row.get("degraded_reason") or "no reason recorded")
450	   450	        elif st not in SCORING:
451	   451	            reason = "status " + st
452	   452	        elif st == "cap_failure" and self.cap_excluded:
453	   453	            reason = "cap_failure (sensitivity figure)"
454	   454	        elif st != "cap_failure":
455	   455	            if ttype == REVIEW and not isinstance(row.get(CATCH), (int, float)):
456	   456	                reason = "ungraded (defect_catch_rate null)"
457	   457	            elif ttype != REVIEW and not isinstance(row.get(PASS), (int, float)):
458	   458	                reason = "ungraded (hidden_test_pass_rate null)"
459	   459	        row["_valid"] = reason is None
460	   460	        row["_reason"] = reason
461	   461	        cell = self.cells.setdefault((arm, task), {}).setdefault(row["trial"], {"valid": None, "rows": []})
462	   462	        cell["rows"].append(row)

464	   464	    # -- scores
465	   465	    def pass_score(self, row):
466	   466	        return 0.0 if row["status"] == "cap_failure" else float(row[PASS])
467	   467	
468	   468	    def catch_task_score(self, row):
469	   469	        return 0.0 if row["status"] == "cap_failure" else float(row[CATCH])
470	   470	
471	   471	    def defect_vector(self, row):
472	   472	        n = self.task_defects.get(row["task_id"], 0)
473	   473	        if n <= 0:
474	   474	            return None, "none"
475	   475	        if row["status"] == "cap_failure":
476	   476	            return [0.0] * n, "cap"
477	   477	        missed = row.get("defects_missed")
478	   478	        if missed is None and isinstance(row.get("recall"), dict):
479	   479	            missed = row["recall"].get("missed")
480	   480	        if isinstance(missed, list) and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in missed):
481	   481	            ms = set(missed)
482	   482	            return [0.0 if f"d{k}" in ms else 1.0 for k in range(1, n + 1)], "ids"
483	   483	        return [float(row[CATCH])] * n, "rate"
484	   484	
485	   485	    # -- shares
486	   486	    def excluded_share(self, arm):
487	   487	        cells = [c for (a, _), trials in self.cells.items() if a == arm for c in trials.values()]
488	   488	        if not cells:
489	   489	            return None, 0, 0
490	   490	        ex = sum(1 for c in cells if c["valid"] is None)
491	   491	        return ex / len(cells), ex, len(cells)

493	   493	    # -- one paired comparison of `arm` against `ctrl` on one primary
494	   494	    def compare(self, arm, ctrl, metric, seed):
495	   495	        types = (REVIEW,) if metric == CATCH else BUILD_TYPES
496	   496	        tasks = sorted({t for (a, t) in self.cells if a in (arm, ctrl) and self.task_type.get(t) in types})
497	   497	        res = {"metric": metric, "arm": arm, "control": ctrl, "unit": "tasks", "pairs": [], "unpaired": [],
498	   498	               "dropped": [], "diffs": [], "task_diffs": [], "defect_identity": set()}
499	   499	        for task in tasks:
500	   500	            ca, cc = self.cells.get((arm, task), {}), self.cells.get((ctrl, task), {})
501	   501	            drop = sorted(t for t in set(ca) | set(cc)
502	   502	                          if (t in ca and ca[t]["valid"] is None) or (t in cc and cc[t]["valid"] is None))
503	   503	            for t in drop:
504	   504	                for side, cs in ((arm, ca), (ctrl, cc)):
505	   505	                    if t in cs and cs[t]["valid"] is not None:
506	   506	                        res["dropped"].append({"task_id": task, "trial": t, "arm": side,
507	   507	                                               "run_id": cs[t]["valid"]["run_id"]})
508	   508	            va = [ca[t]["valid"] for t in sorted(ca) if t not in drop]
509	   509	            vc = [cc[t]["valid"] for t in sorted(cc) if t not in drop]
510	   510	            if not va or not vc:
511	   511	                why = []
512	   512	                for side, cs, vs in ((arm, ca, va), (ctrl, cc, vc)):
513	   513	                    if vs:
514	   514	                        continue
515	   515	                    if not cs:
516	   516	                        why.append(f"no row in {side}")
517	   517	                    elif all(cs[t]["valid"] is None for t in cs):
518	   518	                        why.append(f"every cell of {side} excluded")
519	   519	                    else:
520	   520	                        why.append(f"the cells of {side} dropped pairwise")
521	   521	                res["unpaired"].append({"task_id": task, "reason": "; ".join(why)})
522	   522	                continue
523	   523	            pair = {"task_id": task, "arm_runs": [r["run_id"] for r in va], "control_runs": [r["run_id"] for r in vc],
524	   524	                    "arm_cost": mean([float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0) for r in va]),
525	   525	                    "control_cost": mean([float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0) for r in vc]),
526	   526	                    "arm_wall": mean([float(r.get("wall_clock_ms") or 0) for r in va]),
527	   527	                    "control_wall": mean([float(r.get("wall_clock_ms") or 0) for r in vc])}
528	   528	            if metric == PASS:
529	   529	                ma, mc = mean([self.pass_score(r) for r in va]), mean([self.pass_score(r) for r in vc])
530	   530	                pair.update(arm_value=ma, control_value=mc, diff=ma - mc)
531	   531	                res["diffs"].append(ma - mc)
532	   532	                res["task_diffs"].append(ma - mc)
533	   533	            else:
534	   534	                ma, mc = mean([self.catch_task_score(r) for r in va]), mean([self.catch_task_score(r) for r in vc])
535	   535	                pair.update(arm_value=ma, control_value=mc, diff=ma - mc)
536	   536	                res["task_diffs"].append(ma - mc)
537	   537	                vecs_a = [self.defect_vector(r) for r in va]
538	   538	                vecs_c = [self.defect_vector(r) for r in vc]
539	   539	                for _, how in vecs_a + vecs_c:
540	   540	                    res["defect_identity"].add(how)
541	   541	                if all(v is not None for v, _ in vecs_a + vecs_c):
542	   542	                    n = len(vecs_a[0][0])
543	   543	                    dd = [mean([v[k] for v, _ in vecs_a]) - mean([v[k] for v, _ in vecs_c]) for k in range(n)]
544	   544	                    pair["defects"] = n
545	   545	                    pair["defect_diffs"] = dd
546	   546	                    res["diffs"].extend(dd)
547	   547	                else:
548	   548	                    pair["defects"] = 0
549	   549	            res["pairs"].append(pair)
550	   550	        if metric == CATCH:
551	   551	            res["unit"] = "defects"
552	   552	        res["defect_identity"] = sorted(res["defect_identity"] - {"cap"})
553	   553	        n = len(res["diffs"])
554	   554	        res["n"] = n
555	   555	        res["n_tasks"] = len(res["pairs"])
556	   556	        res["d"] = mean(res["diffs"]) if n else None
557	   557	        res["lo"], res["hi"] = bootstrap(res["diffs"], self.args.resamples, self.args.level, seed)
558	   558	        res["mde"] = mde(res["diffs"], self.args.level)
559	   559	        res["half_width"] = None if res["lo"] is None else (res["hi"] - res["lo"]) / 2.0
560	   560	        if metric == CATCH:
561	   561	            td = res["task_diffs"]
562	   562	            lo, hi = bootstrap(td, self.args.resamples, self.args.level, seed)
563	   563	            res["task_level"] = {"unit": "tasks", "n": len(td), "d": mean(td) if td else None, "lo": lo, "hi": hi}
564	   564	        return res

566	   566	    def deltas(self, comps):
567	   567	        """c and w over the per-task means of the cells the primaries paired."""
568	   568	        per_task = {}
569	   569	        for comp in comps:
570	   570	            for p in comp["pairs"]:
571	   571	                per_task.setdefault(p["task_id"], p)
572	   572	        if not per_task:
573	   573	            return None, None, 0
574	   574	        ps = [per_task[t] for t in sorted(per_task)]
575	   575	
576	   576	        def delta(a, c):
577	   577	            ma, mc = mean([p[a] for p in ps]), mean([p[c] for p in ps])
578	   578	            return None if not mc else (ma - mc) / mc * 100.0
579	   579	
580	   580	        return delta("arm_cost", "control_cost"), delta("arm_wall", "control_wall"), len(ps)

582	   582	    def decide(self, arm, comps, c, w, share):
583	   583	        T = float(self.rules.get("threshold_points", 0.03))
584	   584	        C = float(self.rules.get("cost_lower_pct", 15))
585	   585	        P = [p for p in comps if p["n"] > 0]
586	   586	        nopair = len(P) < len(comps)
587	   587	        name = lambda p: p["metric"]  # noqa: E731
588	   588	        if share is not None and r9(share) > self.guard:
589	   589	            # DEC-0393: the degradation guard reads first, whatever the interval (lead's ruling, Sprint 260)
590	   590	            clause = f"excluded share {share:.3f} > {self.guard:g}"
591	   591	            return "inconclusive", f"inconclusive (degradation guard, evaluated first): {clause}", [clause]
592	   592	        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["lo"]) > 0]
593	   593	        if hits:
594	   594	            return "investigate", f"investigate: any applicable primary has lo > 0 ({', '.join(hits)})", []
595	   595	        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["d"]) < -T and r9(p["hi"]) < 0]
596	   596	        if hits:
597	   597	            return "keep", f"keep: any applicable primary has d < -{T:g} and hi < 0 ({', '.join(hits)})", []
598	   598	        clauses = []
599	   599	        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["d"]) < -T]
600	   600	        if hits:
601	   601	            clauses.append(f"d < -{T:g} ({', '.join(hits)})")
602	   602	        if nopair:
603	   603	            clauses.append("no valid pair (" + ", ".join(name(p) for p in comps if p["n"] == 0) + ")")
604	   604	        if clauses:
605	   605	            return "inconclusive", "inconclusive: " + "; ".join(clauses), clauses
606	   606	        cost_ok = (c is not None and r9(c) <= -C) or (w is not None and r9(w) <= -C)
607	   607	        if all(r9(p["d"]) >= -T for p in comps) and cost_ok:
608	   608	            which = []
609	   609	            if c is not None and r9(c) <= -C:
610	   610	                which.append(f"c = {c:+.1f}")
611	   611	            if w is not None and r9(w) <= -C:
612	   612	                which.append(f"w = {w:+.1f}")
613	   613	            return "remove", (f"remove: every applicable primary has d >= -{T:g} and "
614	   614	                              f"(c <= -{C:g} or w <= -{C:g}) ({', '.join(which)})"), []
615	   615	        return "simplify", f"simplify: every applicable primary within -{T:g}, cost similar", []

617	   617	    def arm_report(self, arm, cuts, seed):
618	   618	        prims = self.primaries(arm)
619	   619	        comps = [self.compare(arm, CONTROL, m, seed) for m in prims]
620	   620	        c, w, n_cost = self.deltas(comps)
621	   621	        share, ex, seen = self.excluded_share(arm)
622	   622	        out = {"arm": arm, "arm_label": self.arms[arm].get("label", arm), "primaries": prims,
623	   623	               "comparisons": comps, "c": c, "w": w, "cost_tasks": n_cost,
624	   624	               "excluded_share": share, "excluded_cells": ex, "cells_seen": seen}
625	   625	        if not seen:
626	   626	            state, rule, clauses = "no_rows", "no rows for this arm", []
627	   627	        else:
628	   628	            state, rule, clauses = self.decide(arm, comps, c, w, share)
629	   629	        out["predicate_state"] = state
630	   630	        out["predicate_rule"] = rule
631	   631	        label = DISPLAY.get(state, state)
632	   632	        if state == "inconclusive" and any(cl.startswith("excluded share") for cl in clauses):
633	   633	            label = "Inconclusive-by-degradation"
